Strings.smoothScrollCaption: Turns each mouse wheel step into a short, gentle glide. The touchpad is not affected.
Strings.scrollTrackpadNote: The touchpad is untouched: it keeps the scroll direction set in Windows Settings.
mouseExceptions.captionScrollDirection: The wheel keeps the direction Windows gives it in these apps.
mouseButtons.spacesEnableLabel: Switch desktops by dragging a button
mouseButtons.spacesEnableCaption: Hold the chosen button and drag: left or right moves one virtual desktop over, up opens Task View. A short click still does what it always did.
mouseButtons.spacesFollowsDragCaption: Dragging right brings the desktop on the left, the way a touchpad swipe carries it along with your fingers.
quitProtection.accessibilityCaption: Protection watches only Alt+F4, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+W and Ctrl+F4. Apps that run as administrator are out of its reach and stay unprotected.
quitProtection.enabledCaption: Other shortcuts continue to work normally.
win.input.mousePageDescription: Fixes for worn buttons, gentler wheel scrolling and the wheel direction. Touchpads keep their Windows settings.
win.input.wheelHeuristicNote: Only whole notches of a mouse wheel glide. Touchpads and high-resolution wheels keep their own smooth scrolling.
win.input.elevatedNote: Windows of apps that run as administrator are out of reach: these fixes do not apply while such a window is in front.
win.input.extraButtonsHint: Windows delivers only the Back and Forward side buttons and tilting wheels. Buttons 6 and up need your mouse's own software.
win.input.pendingShortcutHint: Click the field, then press the key combination.
win.input.debounceRepeatNote: Holding a key still repeats it: presses that last past the keyboard's repeat delay are never filtered. Modifier and lock keys are never filtered.
win.input.superOfficeKeyWarning: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Win is the Office key: on its own it opens Microsoft 365, and with W, X, P, O, T, N, D, L or Y it opens Office apps, which then never see those keys.
win.input.superAltGrNote: Ctrl+Alt works as AltGr on many keyboard layouts, so some Super key combinations may type characters such as € or @.
win.input.superElevatedNote: Apps that run as administrator don't see the Super key. If you release it while such a window is in front, the held modifiers are let go within a few seconds.
win.input.quitSlotTitle: Alt+F4 · close the window or quit the app
win.input.closeSlotTitle: Ctrl+W · close the tab or document
win.input.quitSecondChordCaption: Ctrl+Q quits some apps. In others it does something else, such as marking mail as read.
win.input.closeSecondChordCaption: Ctrl+F4 closes the document or tab in many apps.
win.input.extraConflictCtrlShiftW: Chromium browsers close the whole window with Ctrl+Shift+W.
win.input.extraConflictAltShift: Alt+Shift switches the keyboard language on many PCs.
